El Salvador
Maria Conchita gave birth to her baby on the escape trail they all followed, then she stood up with it and followed the others. Each carried their worldly goods, most with a belt tied around and carried over the shoulder or under one arm. When they rested under a small tree on a level place on the mountain, she tried to nurse it but the milk was not ready, the baby was only 30 minutes old. The infant tried to cry but did not know how yet. After fitfull sleep under the whump whump whump of the helicopters they ate what little they had cold, then trudged on to the secret cave and under lantern light where Dr. Clement stayed. Thorn scratches, infected mosquito bites, abrasions from loose gravel - bandages were needed, but the soldiers were told possessors of bandage cloth or bandaids were communists and to protect El Salvador needed to be destroyed. Usually just one slug, then dragged to the edge of town or the edge of the trail to stiffen in death in the blazing sun. So they started to use mosquito netting where they could find or steal it, and then those with mosquito netting began to disappear, and sometimes would be found in the weeds in the hills a week or two later when the stench of death reached the village. So then somehow they got diapers, anywhere, clean cloth for bandages, and so Maria Conchita, as she left a bus with her baby and a package of 5 diapers and she did not have the stamp mark on her I.D. paper she kept in her sweaty shoe, so they knew she was a rebel and they arrested her and screams behind the bus, then a shot and she was silent and only the crying of the baby was heard, and then there was another shot, and then there was silence. Dr. Clement estimated 40,000 had died in El Salvador in his 3 years there and the helicopters with machine guns and the tiny spotter planes with rockets could glide low and fire into any group of quiet thin men and women and children and babies would be killed because only rebels were in the hills like that. And if they tended their crops, they knew they were rebels, because everyone else had left their land and gone into the cities. If you stayed on your land, it meant that you supported the rebel army in the hills, so you should be killed to help save the country. At least that's what the military said the U.S. advisers told them, while all this time Americans were going to football games on Saturdays in the United States and to church on Sunday and were proud to be who they were, although they could never save any money because of big hospital bills and the children in big programs that cost a lot of money, and most thought El Salvador was the name of a church in Mexico or somewhere, and that was all, and the El Salvador generals were rich and knew a lot of Americans. But, but . . . , but . . , none of this was terrorism, it was all just fighting the enemies of the free world.

Guatemala
"To watch the sunrise after a night of fullness with you. To think that by the time the cock crows the last time at dusk, and the donkey brays at the heated night, the stars moistly glistening, by then? the new life in you will have become our dark- eyed child, to give us both the fragrance of our seed, our shared perfume, our pollinating night on earth alone-" So many lines of gentle imagery you wrote, my son. You showed them to us all, unsurely. Where did such lines begin? Where were their origins? Where is a poet's will? Today I saw something of the roots of words you wrote. Your concave wrists, all soaked in blood, the tendons pearly white that signalled to the pencil in your hand, to write your words on grimy sheets - sweaty, stained, your severed hand stinking in the grass, with pearly nubs and clotted flies, with all of you - your mutilated manhood, before they severed it and stuffed it in your mouth. Oh, my God! Even Satan never did this thing to anyone. What a fiendish hell this "native land" of ours has once again become, with black and bloody soil, made so by those we thought we knew, who do these deeds like men gone mad, like bounty hunters who never wrote a poem in their lives, who never read a poem in their lives, or did they? before this lunacy hid the sun and severed all ourselves...

Soft targets
Soft targets in the struggle for control we strike soft targets first - in Nicaragua, and everywhere else where the people are getting uppity. Soft targets first, most of all and last. Bombs in schoolrooms, we pay somebody to do it. Plenty of folks that will do it, their kids need everything. Poisoned candy for the Indians of the Amazon. Castrated priests, we can arrange all this. Plastic bombs in baby carriages, nuns whose vaginas have been scoured with machetes in mountain villages to make way for investments to keep wages paid by profitable businesses low, get wages down at home. If profits are good at 60 cents an hour then they'll be better at 20 cents. Get our cash flow better, to set aside for takeovers and golden parachutes but get the vulgar ones who complain write poetry on prison walls, protest against our care we stand for freedom everywhere, but remember go after the softness. Go after easy ones, to change the atmosphere, let there be blood in the air, dead babies in the streets, behind the houses, once in a while make it look like "they" did it to themselves, truth itself is an easy soft target. Soft targets easily strangled to soften the valley the mountain passes dead women to soften husbands, kidnapped villagers murdered by police teach lessons to surviving soft targets, out in the public burned buildings, pillage soft targets. poison toothpaste and cigars for Fidel, publish CIA papers blame soft targets for their fates, plant lies and contraband to twist the minds of everyone to hide the truth from everyone to make soft targets of everyone of the earth turn the ferment from itself poison it with lies about the purposes of honorable revolutionaries who seek to break the grip of the deathly past. Honor is a soft target, trust between people in this continent is a soft target we must turn our victims' hatred toward each other. Leaflets from our planes saying anything to twist the minds of soft targets before we fire secret guns at their presidents, buy their parliaments at the market price, restore their shahs, their czars, their kaisers, their kings of Kuwait who serve us well we cannot care we destroy soft targets cut off testicles and heads in the night in the backs of Spanish-speaking police stations, sever hands suspend upside down with their heads in tubs of water - all in the name of the American way - the stubs of fingers, before their hands are around our throats snarling in our ears foul hard targets foul empire builders foul spoilers of our lives foul spoilers of our world we are no longer soft targets we did not want targets, soft or hard we wanted to love you and you to love us to be honest with each other, honesty - one of the highest forms of love you are our hard targets now, it was your idea. We would not kill your wives your mothers your babes as you have done to us for we are humanity speaking 2000 languages, we can be dammed up but not for long, not forever, our river is indestructible. You "railsplitter" that Neruda appealed to, who now turns out to be a builder of guillotines, not fence rails. When once we know who and what you are we will not believe your words, no longer trust your handshakes, you who see us as soft targets, you who are lost you who think of commodities and become commodities you who have declared soft target war against trees, against mineral deposits you who use beautiful beaches to test your armed landing craft you who have done such violence to us as we would never do to you. Soft targets, yes you who would make us soft targets, you who would make the defenseless world itself a soft target, a great target, you who think of targets square round targets, female-shaped transparent opaque oblong bell-shaped targets, targets targets always targets. Are your family members "targets"? Are your children targets in your scheme of things ?

BOOK III — I Am Writing of Handgrenades, Butterflies and Kisses
The ghosts of Playa Giron
Remember - Primitivo, Jose, Carlos, Crecencio, Dagoberto and Raul . . . it was hot hot that morning - as it always is at Playa Giron and you were worried, there was news of bombs at Ciudad Libertad and Santiago our planes - our 9 planes, the radio crackles, but something's at the coast - here at Playa Giron, los gusanos, the gusanos! down the narrow roads in little trucks it is always hot, your guns and gear your heart pounding your hands chilled in the heat, They came ashore at 4 AM, it's 9 AM now. It's on us, the militia. The Army - where are they? It's on us! My heart is pounding. I hear guns ahead, mortars, and then - the cottages, the beach beyond get on the ground, off the road! Hide! the cottages, a machine gun by the dining hall, 2 dead floating in the pool bloody streaks theirs? ours? Get low, get back, hide! There they are. Fire! Crash! Darkness. Hot place on my temple, burning sensation, My vision is dark gray. I hear faint voices. I hear no voices. It is dark D a r k. D a r D a Primitivo! Oh, Primitivo! Run! Get back! Julio, Crecencio, Dagoberto, Rufino, Pedro, Raul get back! The Army came, finally at 1 PM, to help us out. Fidel is here! Fidel! It is midnignt. Oh, god think of those of us who are lost. Primitivo, from my town. . . . We are exhausted. We need sleep, someone sings Adelante, Cubano - softly, in the night. The pale light of dawn. Pink clouds. Rifle fire before dawn. Smoke - explosions, groans and blood. We're gaining. It is hot again. Our wounded we are taking prisoners. Look at them! U.S. Army clothes. Unsmiling, looking at the ground, limping, hot day at Playa Giron. Always hot. U.S. weapons. U.S. ships. We sank the Houston, I hear. Never heard of it. Big ship, they say. Smoke and sweat and piss. More prisoners - always hot. Our armor moves up. We're taking it back. Almost over. Hot, always hot. Drive these gusanos into the sea; this filth that violates us. These sons of the rich, sons of the privileged, these sons of landowners, these batistianos, these murderers of our dreams, of our lives, these scum . . . And so I learned the story of Primitivo and the others - who died. and I had lived a day - an invitado - at Playa Giron - a month before their deaths. One month! before Primitivo died, and his vision grew dark in the heat, and all sound softened into silence in his ears, as it did for Julio and Crecencio, Dagoberto, Rufino Pedro and Raul, for the beast they fought is the same I fight and fear and despise and am in the belly of - and would chain once and for all in history's museum of memories and so, Primitivo and Raul and Pedro and all the others of the 156 who died, we have different homelands but I tell you myself that you fought for me and for others around the world, this tiny world and its tiny history but that was large enough to encompass giant Playa Giron and its struggle against the dragon of the world, and your Apollo-like heroism, your Minerva-like committment to love and laughter, and children in the park and babies smiling on our laps. Thank you deeply Primitivo and Crecencio and Dagoberto and Raul and Enrique, those two hot days gave you forever a place of memory in ourselves and in the memories of our hemisphere - and we will tell your story every time we fear and are in doubt, the story of those days of long ago, of 30 years ago, those courageous days, those hot days of April 1961.

The world situation
Dated June 12, 1991. The U.S. has everyone by the balls at the present time, just like the Medes, the Persians, the Greeks, the Romans, the Egyptians, and the Mongols did in their turn. . . . .
BOOK III — I Am Writing of Handgrenades, Butterflies and Kisses
These cities of the damned
They died in their decade in their century seeking fresh water, loving arms, holding children and other lovers through the night, rest and peace and honor for everyone in every place every boy and girl every gorgeous woman every grizzled elder, that they all might feel the warmth of love the comfort of shelter the excitement of passion of mating in the midst of pillows on great beds, of laughter on merry-go-rounds in every neighborhood. Of picnics by white crystal streams, symphonies, 2-act plays, 3-act plays, music, poetry at dawn and at midnight, children's choruses, grandmothers with healthy skin and friendly smiles, all this beauty god-like from the goddess, like fragments and portions of life on every beach, on every flower with every butterfly on every ornamented slope. In every language, every skin color, wrinkled brow, every child with permanent teeth. Yet in spite of all this, the 500,000 in 1965 floating dead down rivers in Indonesia, on portions of every continent, every island, the headless bodies of young boys, blood-stained thighs of dead young girls, skeletal remains of starved brown-skin babies all dead behind screams and moans -- caused by the troops, the tanks the bombardments, poison gases, the torpedoes, rockets, depth bombs, the shards of hell spraying in every innocent village where copper or iron ore are underground nearby. With machine guns mounted on Jeep Cherokees and grimy torture chambers behind stucco walls near the ruins of ancient Aztex, Maya or Inca civilizations. Then to kill in 20 minutes with poisons both orange and green, to get the peasants hauled away by earth-moving monsters that can push over giant trees 2000 years old when necessary; or scrape peasants and villages to the side. So for the present the deadly power wins, with all the murdered ones disposed of, those who dreamed and played guitars and flutes for children, and combed the hair of lovely elders in rest homes. These most lovable of ourselves, that had to be eliminated for the sake of profit and enterprise - erased, murdered gotten out the way, out of the way of profit-making machinery that tears up, grinds out and pummels paper dollars into savings accounts. So all the removed, the dispatched, the cancelled, the erased, the dead, their echoes of laughter, music and gorgeous dancing now haunt the paths and alleys of these cities, these heroic cities of the murdered, these cities of the damned.
BOOK III — I Am Writing of Handgrenades, Butterflies and Kisses
Those who play guitars must win
There is so little time for music in our veins - only 60 or 70 or 80 years and so many are tearing the veins of the world out by the roots, as they tear guitar strings out with military equipment meant for the purpose. Conquer a people's music and you conquer the soul of their world. You strip off the harmonies of the people and you drink their blood while they play love songs late at night in public parks or on beaches beside the soft lapping sound of baby waves. Those who play guitars must win. You seek to silence ordinary sounds of ordinary people making ordinary love in ordinary places to the caresses of octaves and arpeggios softened by candlelight while the Souza troops goosestep into a bleeding military future. Those who play guitars must win. But those of us who cry through flutes and violins and guitars have such long histories. We are like sinewy rock formations that endured every fiery heat and have emerged with the beauty of our layers intact, and we have survived. Those who play guitars must win. We again beat drums beat drums sing angel choruses that will deafen cannons and turn them into themselves to explode in their own mouths, within the hearing of lovers singing choruses of songs from Venus, heated Mercury, the lonely moons of Saturn and Neptune from all the spaces of the goddess. Those who play guitars must win. Ours is the goddess that would seize the ears of juvenile bullies and twist them til they throw down their guns and they will then pray for help from singers and minstrels who told their tales for centuries through the wars that left military heroes ground into the sands of ancient cities. Those who play guitars must win So the great cries of life in every key, accompanying every dance, every whirling gripping movement of making love to our own music we give the world. The love that is our music, the music that is our love, with finally no room left for military dismemberment of fools in their pride of state so foully seeking dominion over guitars guitars safe with everlasting life, to let those who play guitars be heard. Those who play guitars must win.
BOOK III — I Am Writing of Handgrenades, Butterflies and Kisses
50 bullets in a Persian poet
He dared to see a red sunset and call it red. He dared to view the stars and wonder what their fire was. He dared to see a woman's veil and wonder why. He dared to wonder about the secret police. He wondered why he and his beloved could not touch in public. Who said it should be so? Why was his friend Feras hanged from a bridge girder for protesting unemployment in the square? Why, oh why? He wondered, and wrote and published. But one night, they came and took him, and tortured him, and at dawn placed many bullets in him, then more and more, til 50 bullet holes taught lessons to others viewing his rotting body tied just there, beneath his poetry nailed above, with bullets through his words. But many hesitated, to read those words - furtively, and began to write fresh words, furtively, and look about to see who could be trusted to share them - furtively. And so, here I am, without bullets in my chest or face or arms, with a memoriam of words for a Persian poet of my own time, . . . , who so eloquently - speaks to us from his 50 tiny mouths.
BOOK III — I Am Writing of Handgrenades, Butterflies and Kisses
Tyrannosaurus capital
All the cells in a dinosaur's body are innocent. They don't know what the whole body is doing. Even brain cells don't realize things - individually. No single brain cell ever had its own thought all by itself, a thought not shared with other cells. It's toughest of all in the case of Tyrannesaurus Rex. His and her name means the king or queen of tyranny. Gigantic teeth to rip hearts and stomachs and eyeballs out of more peaceful reptiles back in the Mezozoic, in their own hundred million years before little egg-eating mammals the size of a dog or a pig came along or some super-meteorite that collided with earth and threw up dust that gave them the first nuclear winter at 40 below or both happened - maybe. Remember pictures you've seen of Rex, teeth a foot long made of dentyn and enamel and whatever else teeth are made of - all of individual cells that can't see or understand or hear, maybe they can feel - like a toothache. Some tooth cells are on the cutting edge - like stock brokers in Tyrannesaurus Capital. Making deals, setting up buyouts, first of Ma and Pa's Waffle House on Spring Street, because the land was valuable and the old dump would be torn down - gobbled up. Then buyouts of capital companies, lightbulb companies, tractor companies, wheat marketing companies, then capital countries, like England, Brazil, Russia, Yugoslavia and Japan. Buy them ! Now, before somebody else does ! And not one cell knew the consequences, a cell in a Rex tooth holds firm to do its job - to help the whole system devour an agricultural country, a whole vegetarian brontesaurus. Every cell wants to survive and get a paycheck so it can cell-divide and keep in shape. Cells want to survive - like us. We're cells. Our white blood cells have to give their lives, like soldiers to save the whole body, and they're as ignorant of the politics and economics of the body as soldiers are ignorant of the body politic. But you see, a whole flesh-eating capital heavy country can do incredible damage to others, and to cells in its own body, but it's like tides or glaciers, you can hardly see what's happening. You as a cell can't tell, you're just trying to survive. But your whole dinosasur -- your whole country may be a tyrant, a gangster, a bloody butcher, a cannibal, an executioner in the world of other huge beings, of other huge systems. But you're just a cell, in muscle or brain or tooth tissue and you just want to survive. You have no global view of the behaviour of the dinosaur system of which you are a part with the blood and gore of others dripping down the teeth down the very tooth where you are - where you are a stock broker, a lawyer, a soldier or a certified public accountant on the cutting edge. You are a cell in, a citizen of Tyrannesaurus Capital, perhaps the last giant system, the last dinosaur before extinction.
BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
A Shoshone drum
The voice of a Shoshone drum is the heartbeat of native peoples, of every age, every century, every place. It is the pulse of every animal in the earth, the surge of sap in every tree, to tell us to be faithful to the rhythm of the rains, the rivers, the coming of the sun, the passing of the sun, the coming of the moon. In our knowledge we are lost unless we listen to the wisdom of the trees, the wisdom of the animals in the earth and in the seas.
BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
Harper's Ferry
The remains of this gap in the Blue Ridge Mountains, 2 mysterious rivers, the Shenandoah and the Potomac, with slanted sheets of rock in their rapids, between black cliffs. The body of John Brown still hangs from his gallows at this place, who fought slavery too soon, who seized this place, this arsenal of guns and cannons too soon, with too few men -- to be the signal for revolts by slaves before they learned to read. This intersection of all the fates of earth, of life and death, of million-year-old cataclysms that took place before man learned of this dread place, this Harper's Ferry. This long dead python snake Chesapeake Canal since 1824, in disuse since 1924, with these rivers and cliffs like sentinels watching colliding armies, this carving out with knives and guns the illness of a nation built on living death for Africans for 300 years. This place, this awesome place of historic, dreadful worlds . . . . This Harper's Ferry . . . .
BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
Women in prison, it serves them right...
Children don't behave worth a damn, so it serves them right to have their mothers in prison. It serves the mothers right, they stole baby food from a 7-11 store. It serves them right, they never bothered to get an education and get some skills, especially when they lost their jobs when their corporation employer they washed windows and vacuumed carpets for before they closed down and moved to Mexico. Then when her boy friend got drunk and got arrested and she couldn't pay the rent or work with two kids and she ended up on the streets doped with some crack a "friend" gave her before he screwed her. So it's not the system's fault. It never heard of her. And the corporation? - she was unknown, she was just a window washer. They never heard of her either - not really. So she was bad news, a real loser and she hardly spoke English. Lock her up so she'll get some food and shelter and can't get drugs because she was so depressed - here in the home of the brave and the land of the free - and she'll be able to work in the prison making plastic cups or papers clips at 40 cents an hour - that's better than nothing. And there's medical care, over at Chowchilla and it's only 36 miles and she can make an appointment when she can afford a phone call and can just go right on over when she can get a seat on the bus - so what the hell, she's way better off in prison - right? Menstruation in prison? They know about it. They'll send a man guard around with 10 or 20 tampons, who probably won't make a snide remark. But just think, when you have no control over the processes of your life, suppose your period is a huge one or you have a yeast infection, or diarrhea or bleeding gums, or a kidney stone, you might as well be a carton of old books, or an old jacket with holes in the elbows, that's about as important as you are, when you're in prison. How do you use a vibrator in your sexually-deprived life? How do you read up on child care? How do you get postcards to send to your children you haven't seen since a year ago April? How do you do anything that is beautiful, that is human? that will help you function and make a living when you're back outside? Well, at least you can work for corporations now while you're in prison. You can assemble electronic parts, raise pigs, make license plates, do telemarketing, stuff mattresses, slaughter ostriches for their feathers, be reservation clerks for TWA Airlines so they can transfer clerks to flight attendant jobs to break a flight attendant strike. And your wages? Minimum or less. $4.25 or less, but after deductions they take home about 95 cents. At least it's more than in Latin America or eastern Europe or Asia, those great continental global prisons. Then some prisons charge rent from prisoners making money on the outside. Can you believe it? BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
Ozzie's Place
Not too many investors have tuna salad sandwiches prepared by hand with a teaspoon, stirred on a narrow counter's edge... There's no "futures" in it. How do you capitalize a grilled cheese and a milkshake made the old-fashioned way? by hand... by a little man who laughs with the customers like our grandparents did decades ago? There's nowhere near enough profit in this operation, and too many jokes and too much laughter at lunchtime, and it's not very dignified... Obsolete home-made salads made by an obsolete little man at an obsolete soda fountain in an obsolete pharmacy in obsolete Elmwood, with an obsolete shoe repair shop and an obsolete appliance repair shop down the street; where you can really get your toasters and flatirons and electric fans fixed by obsolete guys who look for obsolete parts - instead of telling you to trash the old thing and get the new one with 24 buttons and computer chips to do the job... But back to Ozzie's place - Somebody ought to modernize things so 20 hamburgers can be fixed at once on an IBM computer oven with old women in tacky uniforms at minimum wage, serving lines of folks with Have a Good Day, and nobody laughing and nobody knowing anybody, but maybe it will be so profitable that Ozzie's place could be franchised and go nationwide. Then it will be worth buying by an insurance company or an investment group, and maybe even be exported to China and Australia and Las Vegas and Milpitas and serve millions and make millions, and finally be big time for Ozzie's place - instead of just people meeting at Russell and College because they know each other and want to have a deeply rich hour together in the middle of the day - So...., Ozzie's like me, with his little containers of sandwich spreads and his spoons and his apron and his slightly bent-over figure making things; lovingly... like he was massaging them to bring them alive...

BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
The prison system
He entered the prison system when he was three days old, when for the first time his mother didn't have enough milk for him. He insisted with her but to no avail. She held him but her milk was watery and thin. He sucked once he found where it was but it quickly became desperate and he clamored and vomited and twitched and wet his pants but there wasn't much there. Already the world was forbidding and not nourishing. Who could he turn to? Where was love and nurturing? In his mother's breast? Her love was thin and watery, that's all he knew. He learned early to survive, to look over his shoulder to doubt her - to not trust him - to not trust her - to doubt him, to learn he would have to take everything, and yet there remained a little pocket of poverty in his soul, at his very center, like a pustule inner tumor filled permanently with poisonous brown fluid never to heal its walls to harden but to always give off signals to the rest of him - like radiation - controlling his mind and nervous system dictating the language that would form and he would use controlling fearing hurt - tears - loss before he started loss before he ever had loss before he was before his birth loss.. loss.. loss.. no trusting only using everyone anyone I'm okay he would say I know what to do. I can make it big. I'll take care of me. I don't need milk I don't need no milk I don't need a mother I don't even know who my dad was, So months passed and he hardly learned to smile, his mother worked til 9 PM earning 3 an hour. Sister giving him one graham cracker for lunch, some peanut butter on a fork he almost strangled on for dinner some milky water - ice cold for Daisy his oldest sister was 8 and all there was for him. At 9:30 his mother finished her glass of wine and cigarette, her angry cursing at her world and at the five of them. She changed his diaper after the wine, sopping wet and stinking since morning, one day it all came off and he spread it everywhere - on the walls, on the refrigerator door. His mother beat him and rubbed his face in it, the only toy he'd had that week, it was his very own, from him... School and fights schoolyard fights every day - blood some times one day a boy was dead in the washroom they accused him because he had just pissed. they let him off but not til after he'd been thrown out of school til the next fall, just when he was learning how to read... At last, thank God for the gang he joined at 14, the Smiling Vipers! He belonged somewhere, at last! Lots of fights some guys dead lots of crack on 57th Street, their turf lots of dough a fancy car at 18 his broad-brimmed hat the gals he helped to make a living, but most of all he helped himself taking care of 'me'. something he learned so long ago, with his mother's milk "I know I killed some guys but they had it coming, coming down from 64th Street and up from 47th Street, and I strangled a couple of females, holding out on me part of the deal was that I would get to fuck them once in a while." but they framed him on a rap he didn't know a thing about he heard the shots but he was pissing in the john, always after he got the clap he only saw the guy outside the can, three guys running down the street, one of them with an Uzi. that great Old Testament persuader from Israel. His fancy lawyer said he'd get him off, but he hasn't seen him since last June. He guessed he wondered what went wrong why all this happened to him He did his best to get himself up near the top he learned real early 'take care of me', he learned it with his mother's milk. But now it looks like they'll be "taking care of me". what went wrong - what went wrong, with me? what went wrong when I was three days old, what went wrong with me?
BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
Old Merritt College
A great temple of life, the young - with laughter now only a burial temple of silence. Moldy silence in the dark tiny leaks of light through weathered places sounds of creatures scurrying in dead debris, dust long silent after girls in oxfords and skirts boys with notebooks hair greased and combed, smiling slightly toward the girls in white skirts and colored sweaters before boarded windows telephones that rang. Laughter in the cafeteria corridors of grime 20 years of grime, water stains students in the library a boy and a girl look at pictures together, all in the dim halls of the past, down the echoing corridors of age and neglect, in what could have been alive with later girls and boys, or symphonies or classes for old people in the neighborhood, or theater, or so much else but no, we are not so equipped to preserve our dear structures from our past. We have other priorities, all born of madness.

BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
I am writing for the Sioux and the wolves.
.... for the 19th century composers writing their passions in unforgettable melodies then going their way; for little crabs that cuddle in our slippers left at water's edge in the doors of little Japanese hotels; for crustaceans warming on heated roads in summer evenings on Cuba's Sancti Spiritu-Trinidad coast, for prairie dogs dozing in underground caverns, in the death journey of salmon - fighting against white rapids to spawn, the eagle in its aerie hovering over two gray eggs, the eels and an octopus that wait gently by their doors for an occasional visitor, for soft brown tarantulas crossing gravel roads in the Mojave seeking shade or protection, for sleek cool snakes who mean only to survive in their uncharitable wild. It is a song of the survival of the warm plasma of life, sustaining gravity, that keeps us home on the surface of the earth that is ours, giving us eggs that become ourselves, our fearful hopeful selves in brief spasms before we move offstage, and let our children on. I am writing for hungry street dwellers who beg in deep chagrin for coins to eat a little, who stand in South African lines from 4 AM for work in deadly mines or shark-infested waters for crumbs for babies. I write the misguided angel chorus of glory for terrified holy men crying out to false gods. The lonely cry from minarets to intercede for souls drying in their veins under the Saharan sun. for all those in distress through history who gave it up and ended it in a suicide in any of the open violent ways - the ultimately most violent deaths of all. I write the ecstasy of men released from prison, the ecstasy of mating men and women lying under the shady tree of knowledge reported on the Rosetta stone and in Maya, Eskimo and Zulu scriptures and finally copied into Genesis. I am writing to celebrate, to announce, to plead for homage from the gods and goddesses for all the little many-legged gods on all the earths everywhere - everywhere near the millions of stars where lives exist. The abundant unbelievably magic beauty of the species in all their forms on land and sea in murky depths, in dizzy alpine crevices housing tiny moss and lichens high above the abyss, in warm dining rooms in cities at the water's edge heated from putrified gases from plankton and pterodactyls living a hundred million years past. I sing for mercy for all the charlatans, the politicians murdering their people in holy battles with young university graduates and husbands dying and cursing with their mouths full of sandy blood - always in a righteous cause and on behalf of God. I sing the international interstellar anthem that drowns the million vulgar national anthems that suffocate and poison us, my song that burns for good all flags that say a line is here and there drawn in the sand to shield our holy selves from vile enemies who are their own holy selves, in their own nations colored on the map. I sing to shout the pain of lies told everywhere to people desperate for the truth, the truth of love. I write to tell of babies of the Sioux, the Pawnee, the Algonquin and the Cree who might have played together bouncing balls or tossing sticks, to share the sun, to share ten sips of water from the creek, except that they were not the same within their parent's eyes. I write to remember ten people on 6 continents in 800 A.D., 40 people farming by a village on the Nile in the time of Ramses; so long decayed when Christ was born; of 12 people dead in Londontown in the bubonic pageant of 1348, their hopes, their loves and fears - dead and unrecalled; one of them a little girl of 8 in rags, who died beside a church. Of all these people - like ourselves, not one whose name we knew, and those who had no name, but felt their breath when someone touched them, who knew a fever's chill, the fear of thunder, the slippery mud under night's curtain in the gloom, with only a tiny oil lamp or two visible in their world that night - who lived a while and thought and dreamed and smiled and laughed and died. I write to celebrate the wolves we've murdered from our fears, those great wild dogs who took us in their trust, when any of us let them. The carcasses of deaths so premature in every geologic epoch - death and death and senseless slaughter and stately executions, and all the billions since the Garden of Eden - whose presence on the earth was a nuisance to someone else, either seeking power or seeking food. I write to celebrate all life in all its wild ways, its crazy shapes, its thousand colors. I am writing for the Sioux and for the wolves. I am white but I am Sioux - I am buffalo, I am wolf, with the wolves I love and know I am writing for the Sioux. I am writing for the wolves.

BOOK IV — The Picture of Dorian America
The Picture of Dorian America
It was a gorgeous portrait of the young republic, as described by the new leaders in the late 1700s.. It had a wide smile, flashing teeth, bright steely blue eyes. The posture was erect, head held high. It was dressed in a proud light blue uniform coat, its long rifle beside it. It was a picture of Dorian America, exhibited by one of the new powerful land owners, an early member of the burgeoning class of money, ownership and power, in this fledgling continent. Years passed, the seasons turned, rivers flooded and horse-drawn carts crossed small bridges in the hills, with oil lamps shining into the night through rough-hewn windows in the villages. . The Indians, the aborigines of the new continent were a shadowy people, lurking in the night, watching the new world being formed. Wagon trains each spring travelled west, wresting more land; forests and plains from Indian tribes. Each year's Thanksgiving was the occasion to visit this Dorian portrait, to enable all to keep the beauty of the country's birth in view, to renew their revolutionary spirit and to look forward into the rising future. Only great leaders of the growing commerce were included in the viewing of the forebear, Dorian. Am I imagining it, but is the mouth beginning to curl into a twisted corner on the left side? I will watch for this, remember, to see if it is true, a twist, so early in the history of the country? I notice others looking startled as they stare into that face, of Dorian, our forefather. So weeks passed and became months and merchants talked with each other amiably in front of their stores and the railroad was pushed through the poorer neighborhood by the creek, and runaway slaves were slipping through town at night heading north and once in a while one was lynched but not very often and the weekly town newspaper kept quiet about it. In the hills of Kentucky and West Virginia coal mines were sunk but casualties were high and they found out about carbon monoxide and how canaries helped but on August 23rd, a hot day there was a mine explosion and 86 workers were buried and it left the families destitute because even when the miners were working their families were in poverty, and the government didn't help because it was a free country, and many could not afford school clothes or shoes for their children and they had to have the kids work in the fields to help pay the bills. Through it all politicians and preachers praised the Lord and the wonderful new free country and they decided on the 4th of July and Washington's Birthday and Labor Day in addition to Thanksgiving. When the 4th of July arrived, they gathered at the room where the picture was. As they walked in, in the dim light - the face, the face . . . gleamed with light brown light but the teeth they were longer, protruding more, with wrinkles around the eyes, the hair and eyebrows needed trimming. The whole group seemed stunned and stood in silence. How could their America look like this? What pact with Satan had someone made? The Baptist preacher and the mayor looked at each other. Neither spoke. Then the mayor turned away and outside he took a deep breath and reminded the others about the parade that afternoon - and be in front of their stores to greet people. It was an important day, to celebrate their growth and their promising future. Nothing was said that day about the Picture of Dorian America. And so, great events came and went, the Civil War, when the theft of Africans from their continent to be free labor for this new paradise democracy, the United States of America, and slavery was abolished, but negroes, African blacks were still being assaulted in every way, cheated, not able to be citizens, to vote, to live in decent housing, but this was never very important in this terrific new country because it was almost never talked about anywhere I t was a good place, towns often said "some of their best friends were niggers". And lynchings, if a young black happened to glance at a white woman, and this was noticed, he might be hanged for rape. Then depressions came, financial panics, but the country always recovered - eventually. Now there were 4 visits to the Dorian America picture, but every time it was different, more disturbing, more deformed, one time the hair was a gray green, the clothing was torn, a front tooth was chipped, it looked like blood on the shirt, the eyes did not shine and were cloudy. Few important people in the town went any more to see the Picture of Dorian America , because it was haunting. They were frightened by the changes they saw - it was black magic. Wars came and went, and veterans were an important part of the population, especially in the 4th of July, and Armistice Day parades celebrating the end of World War I. Then the depression of the 30s, the abject despair after the euphoria of the 20s, families going west in ramshackle old cars, with mattresses and suitcases strapped on the side. Then Roosevelt and his work programs, farm help programs, but these faded after a time, then everything was rescued by World War II. In this war the countries of Europe tore each other to shreds, with the United States relatively untouched, and so could dictate much, but always disguised as to the real intent The Marshall Plan, yes, seemed so magnanimous, but we were not told the ruined countries had to spend the loans with American corporations. So - so - then, the Korean War, after both North and South had crossed the 38th parallel dozens of times, the North was finally lured into invading south and after several years the war approached the Chinese border, where there had been a communist revolution in 1949, so maybe there was a connection. Who knows, because soon it was made clear that East was East and West was West and never the twain, even through the United Nations, crippled by its veto for the powerful ones, could meet. So let's get on with war production because everyone knew we would have to fight our "ally", the Soviet Union, that had borne the brunt of loss, death and damage on our side in World War II, for example, 20 million dead at the hands of the Germans, but that didn't make any difference, we had to protect the world from insidious forces that would change the market economy that we knew worked so well everywhere under our leadership. But then the Russians invaded Czechosovakia, and all we have done since World War II, was invade the Dominican Republic, Grenada, Cuba, Lebanon, to bomb Iraq, get troops in Iran, invade Viet Nam, bomb Cambodia and Laos, overthrow Nicaragua, El Salvador, and Guatemala, kill the presidents of the Congo and Chile, break up Yugoslavia, seemingly doing fine, then get troops in Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia, Montenegro and Herzgovina and, and finally bomb Serbia into the 4th century B.C. Then with sanctions and controlled air space, completely dominate their death squad governments, who in Venezuela and Colombia under U.S. control began the shipments of massive amounts of drugs into American cities to keep American youth from becoming revolutionaries, bomb Panama, and most of all, drive the Soviet Union into bankruptcy trying to keep up with our bombs, our bombers, and nuclear rockets, all aimed at them just in case, of course, always just in case. Our 50,000 nuclear bombs, our 37 submarines each with over 400 nuclear warheads on board, our aircraft carriers, with bombs and planes and torpedoes on all 7 oceans, all weapons of peace, the whole world an armed camp, armed with American weapons, aimed now at everybody. So, finally, after a few years a party of American leaders, with pride wanted to take a look at the Picture of Dorian America. After years of warfare, on each continent, they remembered the Picture. They had not seen it for years. They turned back at the door, in the dim light, for what they saw, oh, I can hardly tell you, what they saw was Dorian America sitting in his place, a submachine gun across his lap, a tank crewman's helmet on his head. His gaunt face and bugged eyes gave him a hideous look, like a warrior from another planet around another star in another time in celestial history, and in the shadows behind him the figure in the dim light of a military tank, its 4 inch gun glowing from the heat of its firings, and swinging around to be aimed directly at us. As soon as we understood, some of us dropped to the ground, others fled through the heavy swinging entrance door into the light of day. Several of them vomited, others ran to the protective railing of the bridge, and looked down, then looked skyward with terrified faces, hardly aware of each other. All looking as though they had had a deep grinding look at Hell. What, what, oh Dear God, what what? What is the truth of all this, what is the Dorian picture trying to tell us? Please, dear God, help us, help us, god oh god . . . Probably all we know, is that it all had something to do with communism, terrorism, Karl Marx, socialism, the free market, investment, the stock market, stolen elections, corporate control of almost all the money everywhere, the rest of us, well, oh what can you expect, we don't matter, it looks like this, maybe in the few years left before it is all over anyway, with all the money burning in hell, great roaring flames as huge mountains of paper money explode and roar in great orange and purple clouds and spread toward every horizon, while there is still time to burn, time to burn, at last, still time to burn . . . Then in the desolation that follows, there is the original pristine portrait of Dorian America, and in the desolation and staggering wreckage of everything everywhere in sight, is the tank commander's figure, [Photograph: a young girl.] `The end of the world?' Yeh, so what? At least it'll be our ball game for the last century. Get out of my face, man. We know what we're doing'.
